definition: Inception is a family of convolutional neural network (CNN) for computer vision, introduced by researchers at Google in 2014 as GoogLeNet (later renamed Inception v1).
details: The series was historically important as an early CNN that separates the stem (data ingest), body (data processing), and head (prediction), an architectural design that persists in all modern CNN.

explainer.lead: Inception is a family of convolutional neural networks for computer vision, introduced by Google researchers in 2014 as GoogLeNet (later Inception v1). It matters historically for establishing the stem-body-head structure that persists in modern CNNs.

tiers.eli5: It's an image-recognition network built in layers, like an assembly line with a starting station, a working section, and a final decision desk.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it as a proven vision backbone for image classification. A pitfall to watch is version drift: 'Inception' covers several generations, so always pin the exact version.
tiers.paperLevel: A CNN family whose central architectural point is separating a stem for data ingest, a body for data processing, and a head for prediction. Later versions extend the original GoogLeNet design.

explainer.example: GoogLeNet (Inception v1) was introduced in 2014 as an early network splitting ingest, processing, and prediction into distinct sections.
